games.name: Afterpull
games.description: Leave a little gravity behind.

wiki.overview: Afterpull is a top-down spatial puzzle in six rooms where the tile you leave behind pulls distant crates. Every step can affect several lines of sight at once, making your own position and the other crates part of the routing problem. The rooms introduce shielding, simultaneous movement, deliberate jams and a final layout with open pits.
rules: Step onto empty floor; you cannot push crates.
The vacated square looks along four cardinal rays and pulls the first visible crate on each ray one cell toward it; walls, crates and your new position block sight.
All pulls use the same starting board. Crates targeting the same destination jam; pulls do not chain.
Fill every gold dock at once to clear a room. Docks do not anchor cargo, and a crate falling into a pit immediately fails the attempt.
There is no clock or move limit. Undo and retry remain available after failure or completion.
controls: Tap WASD/arrows for one cell; holding does not repeat.
Hold Space and tap a direction to preview pulls, jams and pit warnings; release Space, then make a fresh tap to commit.
Z undoes a whole turn; R retries; Enter advances a cleared room.
K/L save/load; Escape pauses; M toggles sound; F toggles fullscreen.

design.rationale:
Each step chooses both a destination and the center of a remote pull. You must preserve finished placements while moving elsewhere, sometimes using another crate as a shield. The satisfying discovery is that a collision can protect two crates through a deliberate jam while a third slides into place.

The closest comparison is magnetic Sokoban: [NABOKOS](https://pixelgrapher.itch.io/nabokos) explicitly uses a magnet to pull boxes onto buttons. Afterpull's proposed distinction is that attraction originates from the square just vacated, automatically affects several unobstructed directions, and supports intentional destination-conflict jams. None of the supplied prior mechanics uses this departure-triggered spatial rule. This comparison does not certify worldwide originality or fun.

games.name: Backstop
games.description: Arrange your runway. Deliver the impossible.

wiki.overview: Backstop is a 2D logistics puzzle across eight cargo bays. A shove gets its distance from the clear runway behind the pusher, so placing a crate or positioning against a wall can be as useful as clearing the destination. Later bays require delivery order, reusable helpers and temporarily removing cargo from a target.
rules: Deliver every crate to a cyan target simultaneously.
A shove travels exactly one cell plus the consecutive clear cells behind you. Walls, crates and edges stop that rear measurement.
Every forward cell must be clear; a blocked shove is rejected in full, never shortened. There is no pulling or chain pushing.
Targets remain normal floor; docked crates can move again and act as backstops.
A NO ROUTE TO GOAL state is recoverable with undo or retry; there is no timer, move cap or rejection penalty.
controls: Arrows/WASD walk one cell and face that way; hold to repeat.
Space shoves the adjacent crate; the runway and landing are shown before the move.
Z/Undo reverses a walk, turn or shove; R/Retry resets this bay; Enter/Next Bay advances a clear.
K/L save/load; Escape pauses; M toggles sound; F toggles fullscreen.

design.rationale:
A crate is both cargo and a measuring tool. Delivering it too early may remove the backstop needed for another delivery. The satisfying discovery is that moving something behind you can fix a landing far ahead. Challenges escalate from fixed wall measurements to installing movable backstops, reusing one crate for several launches and temporarily dismantling a nearly finished solution.

The closest comparison is Sokoban's push-only, crate-to-goal structure ([rules](https://webdocs.cs.ualberta.ca/~games/Sokoban/thegame.html)). Backstop replaces ordinary shoves with exact distances calculated from rear clearance, making cargo placement also configure future movement ranges. Unlike the prior Afterpull mechanic, walking never attracts remote crates or activates vacated cells. Unlike Borrowed Falls, distance is neither captured nor transferred. This is a concrete mechanical distinction, not certification of worldwide originality or fun.

games.name: Corkscrew Key
games.description: A turn is a journey. Six sockets. Unlimited possibilities.

wiki.overview: Corkscrew Key is a 3D spatial puzzle in six chambers built around a rigid five-cube key. A quarter-turn always moves the key one grid unit along the same fixed world axis, so rotation and translation must be planned together. Different arm colors, swept-path previews and optional hints help explain routes through beams, vertical passages and a final vault.
rules: Match the gold socket’s complete position and orientation, not just its center.
Each quarter-turn translates one cell along its selected fixed world axis; reversing direction reverses both rotation and travel.
All five cubes must clear obstacles throughout the turn; an empty landing alone is insufficient.
Blocked moves change nothing. There is no timer, move budget or hazard damage.
Undo or restart freely, and complete six chambers.
controls: 1/2/3 select world X/Y/Z; Right/Left preview positive/negative screw steps; Space executes or advances after docking.
Z undoes a successful move, including docking; R retries.
Right mouse drag orbits; wheel zooms; H toggles an optional next-step hint.

design.rationale:
Every command solves two problems at once: where the key goes and which way its arms point. A move toward the socket can turn an arm into a ceiling beam; moving away can create the orientation needed to return. The central discovery is that rotation order matters: traveling a small loop can change your orientation even though your position stays unchanged. Crisp quarter-turn animations and exact previews make this feel like learning a strange mechanical toy.

The closest comparison is Interlocked's manipulation of blocks in three dimensions, with separate viewing and pulling controls. [Interlocked description](https://www.gpstudios.com/games/view/interlocked). Corkscrew Key instead binds an object's rotation and translation into one signed action; returning to the same position can change its orientation. Among the supplied mechanics, Rotation Relay also uses rotation, but spends stolen angular velocity to turn an arena and redirect gravity. This concept changes only the key's pose, with no borrowed resource, gravity change, gap exchange or perspective scaling. Worldwide originality and fun remain unverified.

design.rationale:
Every move solves two transportation problems at once—or solves one while creating another. The satisfying discovery is treating another cube as a carrier for the height or depth you need. A nearly finished cube may be the only useful partner, making temporary disorder part of a clean final solution. Twin movement trails and synchronized docking clicks make the consequences tangible.

A useful comparison is The Swapper, which creates clones and transfers consciousness between bodies. Crosshaul instead moves two existing objects by exchanging one coordinate, coupling their physical routes. [The Swapper's official description](https://store.steampowered.com/app/231160/The_Swapper/). Among the supplied concepts, Color Custody exchanges behavioral ownership; Crosshaul exchanges spatial components. Perspective Pocket changes placement through silhouette constraints; Crosshaul is independent of camera perspective and preserves coordinate inventories. This appears distinct from the supplied mechanics, but worldwide originality and fun cannot be certified.

design.original_prompt:
The game will simply be called "Feta".

Not prop hunt, but a simple "cat and mouse" style game where the Scientist/Human has a limited amount of time (let's say 5 min default) to kill the rat. The map should be big enough that there is variety and plenty of places for the rat to hide. The rat has a 1 min (default) head start to find a good place to hide. The countdown timer must be discreet.

If the Feta survives the whole time, that player wins. If the scientist kills Feta in that amount of time, the scientist wins.

The main menu must remain simple and allow the players to choose how long they want each round to last and how long the rat should have to hide (defaults are above)

Instead of a variety of maps, stick to making 1 really good map with a variety of assets/props. The map itself has to have a certain theme (suburban home, office space, super market, hospital, school, etc.). Feel free to create new assets/props to make this work. Most of all it needs to feel nice to play on and be fun!

If the rat is hit or shot by the scientist, the round ends and we get to start again and choose our characters. Ensure a round can only start when at least one Feta and one Scientist is selected.

games.name: Gap Flip
games.description: Trade empty space. Find a way together.

wiki.overview: Gap Flip is an offline 2D spatial puzzle spanning ten authored rooms. Select a token and reflect it within the uninterrupted floor corridor on either axis, trading the empty gaps on its two sides. Other tokens help define those corridors, so solving one token may require moving a previously parked helper.
rules: A horizontal or vertical flip lands at first corridor cell + last corridor cell − current cell.
Walls, edges and other tokens bound the corridor; equal side gaps disable a flip for free.
Match all letter-and-color tokens to their goals simultaneously. Goals do not lock or block tokens.
There are no timers, hazards, move budgets or terminal losses; undo and restart are unlimited.
Finish the tenth room after all matches.
controls: Left click a token, choose Horizontal Flip/Vertical Flip, then click the outlined destination ghost to commit.
Undo reverses a committed flip; Restart/R resets only the current room.
Click Next room after solving, then Finish after room ten.
K/L save/load; Escape pauses; M toggles sound; F fullscreen.

design.rationale:
A token doubles as a destination-seeking piece and a movable boundary for its neighbors. You must arrange useful gaps before taking the move you actually want. The satisfying discovery is that temporarily moving a solved token can make an otherwise unreachable landing possible. Exact previews make those dependencies readable.

The closest comparison is Ricochet Robots, where walls and other robots determine stopping positions ([publisher description](https://www.riograndegames.com/games/ricochet-robots/)). Here a token reflects within its available corridor instead of sliding to an obstacle: interior clearance determines its landing, and repeating a flip restores its position while boundaries remain unchanged. Among the supplied prior mechanics, Inside-Out Key also emphasizes empty space, but swaps container contents with surrounding negative space; Gap Flip has no containers or contents exchange. None of the supplied mechanics uses this corridor-reflection rule, and the slug is absent from the supplied list. Worldwide originality and fun remain unverified.

games.name: Odd Matter
games.description: More matter. Less wall.

wiki.overview: Odd Matter is a 3D voxel puzzle in six vaults where overlapping matter can open space. A small drone and rail-bound bars share a 5×5×5 volume: fixed matter contributes one layer and each bar adds another. Bars slide along their marked rails through matter and each other without changing size or orientation.
A moving bar leaves the drone still; if its cell becomes solid, it is crushed.
Guide the drone into the green exit socket. Outer-frame cells always block it.
Z reverses even a crushing move; retry and undo have no timer or move penalty.

A/D moves along X; Q/E down/up along Y; W/S back/front along Z. Each tap is one cell.

design.rationale:
The satisfying discovery is that inserting more solid material can open a tunnel—and inserting still more can close it. Every adjustment changes several places at once. You choose where to park, when to reuse a bar farther ahead, and whether opening a vertical shaft will seal your escape route.

Closest found: [Geometry Overlap](https://www.y8.com/games/geometry_overlap), where overlapping flat shapes cancel while matching a target picture. Here cancellation creates occupied, traversable 3D cavities that must be relocated safely during navigation. Unlike prior Inside-Out Key, nothing swaps between a container and surrounding space; unlike Color Custody, solidity depends on local overlap counts rather than transferred tokens. Worldwide originality and fun remain unverified.

games.name: Peelturn
games.description: Every turn leaves a trace.

wiki.overview: Peelturn is a spatial routing puzzle across twelve compact boards. Launch a packet of beads and each collision deposits a permanent bead, then automatically turns the remaining packet clockwise. Because deposits and waiting packets block later travel, launch order changes the board itself.
rules: Fill every target socket and exhaust every packet.
Only a bead deposited at a stopping cell fills a socket; passing through does not count.
Every collision deposits one bead, then turns the remaining packet clockwise. Deposits become walls and waiting packets block travel.
An initially blocked launch costs nothing. A blocked clockwise exit with beads remaining, empty sockets after exhaustion, or trapped remaining packets loses the attempt.
Undo reverses an entire launch, even mid-route or after loss; retry and undo are unlimited with no timer.
controls: Tab/click selects a packet; arrows aim and preview the first stop; Space launches.
Backspace undoes a whole launch; R retries; Space/Enter advances a clear.
H shows rules; Escape pauses; K/L save/load; M sound; F fullscreen.

design.rationale:
Every impact simultaneously spends one remaining turn and builds a new steering obstacle. A seemingly wasted bead can make a later socket reachable, while filling a socket too early can obstruct another packet. You choose both launch direction and launch order, then watch your plan unfold in a crisp sequence of slides, clicks, and shrinking packets.

The closest comparison is Ricochet Robots, whose pieces slide until obstacles stop them. [Publisher description](https://www.riograndegames.com/games/ricochet-robots/). Peelturn replaces separately chosen movements with a finite automatic route: every collision consumes a bead, creates a permanent stopper, and forces a clockwise continuation. Unlike the prior Impact Orchard, deposited pieces never release stored attacks or activate each other; they change collision geometry. No supplied prior mechanic uses this rule. This comparison cannot certify worldwide originality or fun.

wiki.overview: Embertrail is a controller-first 2D platforming campaign with 32 courses, eight island worlds and eight boss encounters. Mote carries the first spark to free bound guardians, ring the dawn bells and recover the stolen Dawnheart before home freezes. Each course also contains an optional underground route and three moon shards, with regional hazards, lantern upgrades and an original soundtrack.
rules: Travel through 32 courses, free each world’s bound guardian and ring all eight dawn bells.
Collect sparks for extra lights and seek three optional moon shards per course.
Bloom Lantern protects an extra hit and breaks clay; Ember Lantern enables seed casting; Dawn Stars briefly protect against ordinary enemies.
Stomp seed beetles into shells and kick the shells. Bosses expose mint collars during recovery after attacks.
Hold Down at an open root stairway to enter the course’s underground route; release before entering another. Progress saves automatically.
controls: A/D or Left/Right/left stick/D-pad moves; Space/controller A jumps; X/controller X casts with Ember Lantern.
Shift/RT/right bumper runs; S/Down ducks, brakes and enters/leaves root passages.
Tab/controller Y/View opens trail atlas; Escape/Start pauses; arrows/Enter/Escape navigate menus; F fullscreen.

wiki.overview: Harvest Hollow is a cozy 2D farming game about improving a small homestead across changing days. Work the soil, plant and water radishes, carrots and pumpkins, sell the harvest and clear natural debris for building materials. There is no town, combat or deadline, leaving the player free to expand the farm at a comfortable pace.
rules: Crops grow after watered nights: radishes need two, carrots three and pumpkins four. Dry crops wait safely.
Rain waters the whole farm every fourth day; the first three radishes begin watered and ripen after one sleep.
Buy seeds, ship harvests for gold, chop trees for wood, break rocks for stone and clear weeds for bonus seeds.
A sprinkler costs 20 wood, 8 stone and 90 gold; a pond deck costs 18 wood and 5 stone.
The pond refills the watering can; sleeping restores energy. Automatic saves and a manual checkpoint preserve the farm.
controls: Click a patch to walk over and work with Smart tool; 1–7 chooses a specific tool.
WASD/arrows moves; E/Space works the patch ahead; Tab changes crop; I opens the Farm drawer.
N toggles music; M sound; K/L manual save/load; Escape pauses; F fullscreen; R starts a fresh farm.
